title: One boat (Leviticus Rabbah 4:6)
hookLine: a man drills under his own seat in a boat, and the water drowns everyone
tomorrow: why does Hillel call a trip to the bathhouse a mitzvah?

lines: A DRILL, UNDER HIS OWN SEAT.
cards: The boat is already out on the water when someone hears it: a scraping sound, steady, under the benches. Heads turn. One passenger has a drill, and he's boring a hole in the floor, right under his own seat.
What are you doing? He barely looks up. What's it to you?
I'm only drilling under my own place. The others look at the hole, then at the water, then at each other. Somebody reaches for a cup to bail.

teach.b: Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai tells this parable in Leviticus Rabbah, and the passengers' answer is the whole point: the water will come up and flood the boat for all of us. Notice what the man gets right.
It really is his seat. The parable never argues about who owns the spot.
It argues about water, and water doesn't read seat numbers. He isn't even trying to sink anyone. He just thinks the boat ends where his bench does.
Right beside it, the midrash brings a second picture, from a sage named Hezekiah, on the verse "Israel is a scattered sheep."

teach.h: ONE SHEEP HURT, ALL FEEL IT.
teach.b: When one sheep is hurt in its head or a leg, its whole body feels it. So too, the midrash says, when one person in Israel does wrong, all of them feel it.

teach.h: NOBODY IN THE BOAT IS A STRANGER.
teach.b: In the midrash, the boat is the people of Israel, bound to each other. Some readers today hear it more widely too: a team, a family, a town, everyone on one small planet.
Here's the line to repeat tonight: the drill is his, the seat is his, and the sea belongs to everybody. That cuts both ways. It means one person's harm doesn't stay private.
It also means nobody in the boat is a stranger to the others, and patching a hole is everyone's business too.

how: Jewish teaching expresses this as kol Yisrael arevim zeh ba-zeh, 'all Israel are responsible for one another' (Shevuot 39a), and Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai's boat parable is often told to explain it.

o: everyone must row together to get anywhere
what one person does reaches everyone with them
a sinking ship is the captain's job to save

games.q: who's who in the boat — tap the pairs.
p: only drilling under his own seat
the water will flood us all
one sheep hurt, the whole body feels it

s: in the parable, the man is drilling under someone else's seat
he drills under his own place. the seat is his; the water isn't.
the midrash pairs the boat with a picture of a hurt sheep
Hezekiah, on 'Israel is a scattered sheep': one limb hurt, the whole body feels it.
the parable's point is that only the one who does wrong gets hurt
the water comes up for everyone in the boat.

games.q: your roommate says her 2 a.m. music is 'my room, my business.' the walls are thin and you have an exam. by the parable, what's your opening line?
o: 'the parable says what you're doing is a sin, so you have to stop.'
'it's your room, and it's our wall. can we find a time that works?'
'you're right, it's your room. i'll just lie awake and say nothing.'
games.why: the parable grants that the seat is his, then points at the water. her room is hers; the wall, like the boat, is shared.

practice: Stand up and walk slowly for one minute: around the room, down a hall, out the door if you can. Every few steps, name one person your choices this week will touch, and let the list grow longer than you expected.
Then sit for the rest of the bell with everyone who's in your boat.

wordCard.voice: One boat: Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai's parable in Leviticus Rabbah. A hole drilled under one seat floods the boat for everyone in it.

orig.note: Hebrew: a ship or boat, the one Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai fills with passengers.

carryVoice: Your line: we're in one boat. The seat may be yours, but the water is everyone's.

sources.ref: Leviticus Rabbah 4:6 (Hezekiah on Jeremiah 50:17, the scattered sheep; Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai's parable of the man drilling under his place in a boat)
Babylonian Talmud, Shevuot 39a (all Israel are responsible for one another)
